_disclaimer: Curated educational RAG starter dataset. High-stakes numeric thresholds and absolute restrictions are retained only when source-registry policy permits them. Values are not a substitute for the original guideline, laboratory reference interval, diagnosis, or clinician judgment.

danger_threshold: 6.5% or higher is in the diabetes diagnostic range; diagnosis requires appropriate confirmation/context.
dietary_restriction: For established diabetes, carbohydrate quality and quantity should be individualized; emphasize minimally processed, fiber-rich foods and limit sugar-sweetened beverages.

danger_threshold: 126 mg/dL or higher is in the diabetes diagnostic range; confirmation is required when clinically appropriate.
dietary_restriction: Avoid sugary beverages and refined starches; monitor portion sizes of rice, bread, and potatoes.

safe_range: G1: 90 or higher; G2: 60-89 mL/min/1.73m2. These categories alone do not exclude CKD when other kidney-damage markers are present.
caution_range: G3a: 45-59; G3b: 30-44 mL/min/1.73m2. Chronicity/context is required for CKD classification.
danger_threshold: G4: 15-29; G5: below 15 mL/min/1.73m2. A single result does not by itself establish chronicity.
dietary_restriction: Nutrition in CKD is individualized. Sodium reduction is commonly advised; potassium, phosphorus, and protein targets should depend on kidney stage, laboratory values, medications, and clinician/dietitian guidance rather than blanket avoidance.
source: KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline / National Kidney Foundation CKD-EPI 2021 equation

safe_range: Interpret using the reporting laboratory reference interval and clinical context.
caution_range: Mild elevation requires contextual review, including kidney function and medications.
danger_threshold: No single universal emergency threshold is encoded in this prototype; marked elevation or symptoms requires clinician-directed assessment.
dietary_restriction: Do not impose blanket potassium restriction from eGFR alone. Review serum potassium, medications, total intake, and clinician/dietitian advice.

safe_range: under 1500 mg/day for hypertension, diabetes, CKD, or age over 50 (AHA); under 2000 mg/day general population ceiling (WHO, ~5g salt)
caution_range: 1500-2300 mg/day for at-risk patients; 2000-2300 mg/day general population
danger_threshold: above 2300 mg/day for at-risk patients (hypertension/CKD/diabetes); above 4000 mg/day or any single very-high-sodium packaged meal for anyone
dietary_restriction: Limit processed/packaged foods, salted snacks, and sodium-based preservatives (e.g. sodium benzoate, sodium nitrite). At-risk patients (this condition) should use the stricter 1500 mg ceiling, not the general-population number.

safe_range: 7-35 U/L (adult female), 7-40 U/L (adult male), approximate lab-dependent
caution_range: up to 2x the upper reference limit
danger_threshold: more than 2x the upper reference limit
dietary_restriction: Limit fructose-heavy beverages, fried foods, and saturated fat; avoid alcohol entirely.
source: General clinical reference, not independently re-verified

danger_threshold: above 8.5 mg/dL or recurrent gout flares
dietary_restriction: Limit organ meats, shellfish, red meat, and high-fructose beverages; avoid excess alcohol, especially beer.
source: General clinical reference, not independently re-verified

danger_threshold: 160 mg/dL or higher, or above 70 mg/dL with existing cardiovascular disease
dietary_restriction: Limit saturated and trans fats, fried snacks, and palm-oil-heavy processed foods.
source: ATP III categories, not independently re-verified

dietary_restriction: Avoid unpasteurized dairy, high-mercury fish, excess caffeine (above ~200 mg/day), alcohol, and raw/undercooked meat or eggs.
source: General OB guidance, not independently re-verified

biomarker: General precaution (sulfite sensitivity, no single biomarker)
dietary_restriction: 5-10% of people with asthma are sensitive to sulfite preservatives (E220-228: sodium/potassium bisulfite, metabisulfite), which release SO2 gas and can trigger bronchoconstriction. Found in dried fruit, wine/beer, pickled foods, bottled lemon/lime juice, and processed shrimp.

safe_range: saturated fat under 6% of daily calories; sodium under 1500 mg/day (AHA)
caution_range: saturated fat 6-10% of calories; sodium 1500-2300 mg/day
danger_threshold: No universal food-level danger threshold is encoded; overall dietary pattern and individual cardiovascular risk determine targets.
dietary_restriction: Favor an overall heart-healthy eating pattern; reduce saturated fat and excess sodium according to individualized cardiovascular guidance.

Large amounts of raw goitrogenic foods (soy, cruciferous vegetables) can interfere with thyroid hormone production, especially with low iodine intake; cooking largely deactivates this. Calcium, iron, and magnesium supplements should be taken at least 4 hours apart from thyroid medication (e.g. levothyroxine), since they impair its absorption.

safe_range: verified gluten-free foods, under 20 ppm (FDA/Codex Alimentarius gluten-free labeling standard)
caution_range: unlabeled foods with cross-contamination risk (shared equipment/facilities with wheat/barley/rye)
danger_threshold: any food containing wheat, barley, or rye — this is a FULLY RESTRICTED condition, not dose-moderated
dietary_restriction: Strict, permanent, lifelong gluten-free diet is the only effective treatment — there is no safe moderate intake, unlike dose-dependent conditions. Oats are controversial: safe for most, but cross-contamination during growing/milling is common, and a small subset of celiacs react even to pure oats.
source: Codex Alimentarius / FDA gluten-free standard (20 ppm), NYU Langone dietary guidance, cross-checked

safe_range: below 30 mg/g (KDIGO A1: normal to mildly increased)
dietary_restriction: UACR is interpreted with eGFR and clinical context; persistent albuminuria warrants clinician review rather than a diet-only conclusion.
